clue.text: Reversing vehicle, one runs over harmful bugs

indicators.note: in an across clue the letter for one runs on past the end of the harmful word
the clue tells us to turn the vehicle round, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a hired vehicle
ill can mean harmful, as in ill effects
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A reversing car, with someone running over, harms the creepy-crawlies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' here are germs, not insects; 'runs over' means the one comes after the harmful word, running past it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria of rod shape are called by this plural, and germs are colloquially bugs.

clue.text: One composer or another briefly going to Australia

indicators.note: said briefly, the other composer's surname loses its last letter

parts.note: Irving Berlin was a composer of popular songs
Oz is a familiar name for Australia

explanation.surface: A composer, or a shortened other one, heads off to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims BERLIN to BERLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector the French Romantic who wrote the Symphonie fantastique is a famous composer.

clue.text: Way a person's managing on this part of course

indicators.note: in a down clue the managing word sits on top of the rest

parts.note: coping means managing or getting by
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
one can mean a person, as in one never knows

explanation.surface: Someone's way of getting by on a stretch of the route.
explanation.walkthrough: A course here is a layer of bricks or masonry; the coping is the top course of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A masonry piece forming the top layer of a wall belongs to its uppermost course.

clue.text: Embark on pleasure-boat

definitions.meaning: to begin a venture or campaign
a large motorboat used for pleasure trips

explanation.definitionFit: To start up an enterprise is to set it going, and a motor boat for outings has the same name.

clue.text: At camp, no one upset squadron leader's aims

parts.note: under canvas, that is in a tent

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the words no and one upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: Squadron commander's plans are thrown when nobody is in the camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NOI into ION; 'leader's' gives S from squadron.
explanation.definitionFit: Intentions are plans or purposes, things one aims at.

clue.text: English male singer's unknown mission

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An Englishman who sings has a mysterious mission.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission sent to a foreign state.

clue.text: Hairy man taking drug on cutter, so to speak

indicators.note: signals that the letters are to be taken as spoken

parts.note: E is ecstasy, a drug, placed on top of saw, a cutting tool

explanation.surface: A shaggy fellow takes drugs while handling a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: E on top of SAW in a down clue gives E-SAW, which is said like the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob's brother is described as hairy, in contrast to the smooth Jacob.

clue.text: Clan at assembly taken in by such brazenness

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put inside the following word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters are assembled anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A clan meeting is fooled by a shameless display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembly' looks like a noun about a clan gathering, but it signals the rearrangement; 'taken in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Blatancy is flagrant obviousness, a quality of shameless brazenness.

clue.text: It takes any number to make this runner hide!

indicators.note: the runner needs one extra letter to become the hide, so the hide minus that letter is the runner

parts.note: skin is a hide
n is a mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: Needing a crowd before this sledge part can be concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the runner plus N makes SKIN, a hide, so SKIN without N gives the runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow blade on which one glides over snow is a runner.

clue.text: One who surrenders volume from new delivery

indicators.note: the letters are made new by being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gives in over the amount from a fresh consignment.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove V from DELIVERY and rearrange the remaining DELIERY.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way, so one who yields gives in.

clue.text: Louche character's inscription on tomb

definitions.meaning: short for requiescat in pace, rest in peace

explanation.definitionFit: A rip is an old word for a dissolute rascal, and the letters are carved on gravestones.

clue.text: Working railman, true blue

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loyal railway employee on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges RAILMANTRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a deep vivid shade of blue pigment, originally made from lapis lazuli.

clue.text: Blameless as Giovanni Lotario de Conti?

definitions.meaning: the birth name of the pope who took the regnal name of the third of that title in 1198

explanation.walkthrough: Lotario de' Conti di Segni became Pope Innocent III.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means guiltless, and it was also the papal name chosen by Lotario de Conti.

clue.text: Teased for being unkempt

explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is to tease them, and tattered clothes are ragged.

clue.text: Drudge involved in a row once

definitions.meaning: someone made to do hard menial work
a convict who rowed a ship's oars in former times

explanation.walkthrough: A row here is rowing, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict chained to an oar in old warships is the classic image of a drudge.

clue.text: Accommodation you once endlessly conjectured about

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes round the old form of you
the word for conjectured loses its last letter

parts.note: guessed means conjectured
thou is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: You used to wonder ceaselessly about where to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: A guest-house is a small British boarding house, a bed-and-breakfast; 'endlessly' drops the final letter before 'about' wraps the archaic pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hotel or boarding house provides accommodation for paying visitors.

clue.text: Relish on top of zucchini is French

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: est is French for is

explanation.surface: A garnish set on a courgette is a French touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Zucchini is the courgette.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is gusto or enjoyment, which is what relish means here.

clue.text: Powerful Irish novel originally penned in small letters

indicators.note: the short pieces are enclosed in the word for powerful, as if in a pen

parts.note: muscular means strong or powerful
I is the abbreviation for Irish

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter

explanation.surface: A strong Irish novel was first handwritten in lower case.
explanation.walkthrough: IN goes into MUSCULAR. The usual spelling is minuscule; this adjective form also exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuscule letters are lower-case ones, so the adjective describes text written small.

clue.text: Legal principle in which points don't stand up, say

parts.note: E and S are compass points

indicators.note: say tells us the letters merely sound like a word

parts.note: to topple is to fall over, not stay standing

explanation.surface: A rule of law under which arguments collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Estoppel stops a party denying what they earlier asserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Estoppel is a legal doctrine barring someone from contradicting their own previous position.

clue.text: Habit winos somehow get into, showing somnolence

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are put inside the word for habit

parts.note: a habit is a garment, a dress

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Drunks somehow slip into a routine that makes them sleepy.
explanation.walkthrough: A habit is a nun's or monk's garment, hence a dress; 'somehow' and 'get into' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsiness and somnolence both mean sleepiness.

clue.text: Vagrant pinching current set of documents

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the letter is held inside

parts.note: a dosser is a vagrant who sleeps rough
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A tramp steals the latest file of papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dosser is British slang for a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of papers on a person or subject.

clue.text: Greek philosopher initially obsessed with Buddhist school

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker was at first fixated on Buddhism.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Elea is the Greek thinker famous for his paradoxes of motion.

clue.text: Open enclosed bill and behave exaggeratedly

indicators.note: the word for open is wrapped round the bill

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Open a bill tucked inside and make a big fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to ham it up, performing in an exaggerated way.

clue.text: Decorator's band giving report of price-fixing

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the letters echo a spoken word

parts.note: a price freeze fixes prices

explanation.surface: A painter's strip is said to describe controlled prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorative horizontal band along a wall.

clue.text: From Ulster, old substance that doesn't dissolve

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the next words

explanation.surface: Something insoluble from old Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterols such as cholesterol are fatty compounds insoluble in water.

clue.text: Quietly he accepts a pay increase, the hypocrite!

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: the word he takes in the other pieces

parts.note: a rise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: He quietly takes a raise, the two-faced fellow!
explanation.definitionFit: Pharisees in the Gospels are condemned as hypocrites, so the name means a sanctimonious pretender.

clue.text: Cart taking measure of ale to north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a yard of ale is a long glass of beer

explanation.surface: A wagon heads north with a big glass of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to north' turns YARD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low cart, especially a brewer's cart.

clue.text: Ill-timed modern work left by a French female

parts.note: in means fashionable or modern
op is short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship
une is the French feminine for a

explanation.surface: A new work abandoned by a Frenchwoman at a bad moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inopportune means coming at an awkward or unsuitable time.

clue.text: Pole decapitating creature with tusks?

indicators.note: removing the head means losing the first letter

parts.note: a wild boar has tusks

explanation.surface: A pole beheading a tusked beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitating' drops the first letter of BOAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is a pole with a blade used for rowing.

clue.text: Commander's son excluded from heroic story

indicators.note: the son's letter is taken out of the story

parts.note: a saga is a heroic Norse tale

explanation.surface: The commander's boy is left out of the epic.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga is a Turkish commander or chief officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga was an Ottoman title for a military commander or chief.

clue.text: Exchange of shots after game played thus in country?

indicators.note: the exchange comes after the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union
a rally is a long exchange of shots in tennis

explanation.surface: Tennis volleys after a match were played that way in the country?
explanation.walkthrough: 'played thus' links: wordplay played out this way gives the country adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rurally means in a rural way, out in the countryside.

clue.text: A factor's most natural situation

explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component of something, and one feels most at home in one's element.
